## Natural history notes

A small palm-associated moth characterized by narrow brownish wings with pale silvery-white marks, including one larger comma- or exclamation-like mark on the forewing. In Florida, the Palm Leaf Housemaker is found around palms in hammocks, yards, parks, coastal plantings, and other warm habitats, with records from palm hosts such as cabbage palmetto, saw palmetto, and Chinese fan palm. The caterpillars feed on palm fronds from concealed silk-and-frass shelters on the underside of leaves, gradually building chamber-like “houses” as they grow, while adults are nocturnal and may come to lights.
